# Introduction

`diagnosticsTable()` collects the most important diagnostic statistics of a
seasonal adjustment object (created with `perX13()` or `perTramo()`) into a
single data frame. Most of its columns are passed through directly from the
JDemetra+ output — `persephone3` requests a fixed set of user-defined items
(see `userdefined_default` in the package code) and reads them from the Java
result object.

This vignette documents how individual fields of that table are computed.
Currently it covers the overall quality summary (`TotalQ`); further fields
will be documented here as the diagnostics table evolves.

# The `TotalQ` field

`TotalQ` is the value of the JDemetra+ output node `quality.summary`. It is
**not** computed in R: the R side only reads the node from the Java result
and reports it unchanged. A common misconception is that `TotalQ` is based
on the M-statistics Q and Q2 alone — in fact, Q and Q2 are just two of many
tests that feed into it (and, for TRAMO/SEATS, they are not involved at all).

The computation happens in the JDemetra+ output extractors
([`X13Extractor.java`](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdplus-main/blob/develop/jdplus-main-base/jdplus-x13-base-parent/jdplus-x13-base-core/src/main/java/jdplus/x13/base/core/x13/extractors/X13Extractor.java)
and
[`TramoSeatsExtractor.java`](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdplus-main/blob/develop/jdplus-main-base/jdplus-tramoseats-base-parent/jdplus-tramoseats-base-core/src/main/java/jdplus/tramoseats/base/core/tramoseats/extractors/TramoSeatsExtractor.java),
which work identically) in two steps:

## Step 1: Classify each individual test

A fixed list of diagnostic test groups is evaluated, and each individual
test is classified into one of the quality levels `Good`, `Uncertain`, `Bad`
or `Severe` (see
[`X13Factory.java`](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdplus-main/blob/develop/jdplus-main-base/jdplus-x13-base-parent/jdplus-x13-base-core/src/main/java/jdplus/x13/base/core/x13/X13Factory.java)
and
[`TramoSeatsFactory.java`](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdplus-main/blob/develop/jdplus-main-base/jdplus-tramoseats-base-parent/jdplus-tramoseats-base-core/src/main/java/jdplus/tramoseats/base/core/tramoseats/TramoSeatsFactory.java)
for the default lists):

| Test group | X-13 | TRAMO/SEATS |
|---|:---:|:---:|
| Coherence of the decomposition (SA vs. components) | yes | yes |
| Residual tests (Ljung-Box, normality, ...) | yes | yes |
| Out-of-sample / forecasting tests | yes | yes |
| Outliers | yes | yes |
| Spectral test (residual seasonality at seasonal frequencies) | yes | yes |
| Combined seasonality tests | yes | yes |
| Advanced residual seasonality tests | yes | yes |
| Residual trading day tests | yes | yes |
| M-statistics summary Q and Q2 | yes | no |
| Wiener-Kolmogorov diagnostics | no | yes |

The two method-specific groups use the following thresholds:

- **X-13 M-statistics**
  ([`MDiagnostics.java`](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdplus-main/blob/develop/jdplus-main-base/jdplus-x13-base-parent/jdplus-x13-base-core/src/main/java/jdplus/x13/base/core/x13/diagnostics/MDiagnostics.java)):
  Q and Q2 are not p-values but already quality scores — the proportion of
  the M-statistics exceeding their critical value (Q2 excludes M7 from the
  computation). They are classified directly by value:
  - `Q >= 2` → `Severe`, `Q >= 1` → `Bad`, otherwise `Good`
  - the same rule for Q2
- **SEATS Wiener-Kolmogorov tests**
  ([`SeatsDiagnostics.java`](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdplus-main/blob/develop/jdplus-main-base/jdplus-tramoseats-base-parent/jdplus-tramoseats-base-core/src/main/java/jdplus/tramoseats/base/core/seats/diagnostics/SeatsDiagnostics.java)):
  genuine p-values (variance of the seasonal component, variance of the
  irregular component, and their correlation):
  - `p <= 0.005` → `Bad`, `p > 0.05` → `Good`, otherwise `Uncertain`

## Step 2: Aggregate to an overall quality

The classification of all individual tests is combined by
`ProcDiagnostic.summary()`
([`ProcDiagnostic.java`](https://github.com/jdemetra/jdplus-main/blob/develop/jdplus-main-base/jdplus-toolkit-base-parent/jdplus-toolkit-base-api/src/main/java/jdplus/toolkit/base/api/processing/ProcDiagnostic.java)):

1. If **any** test is `Error`, the overall result is `Error`. Otherwise, if
   any test is `Severe`, the overall result is `Severe`.
2. Otherwise the mean score over all interpretable tests is formed, with
   `Good = 3`, `Uncertain = 2`, `Bad = 0`:
   - mean `>= 2.5` → `Good`
   - mean `>= 1.5` → `Uncertain`
   - otherwise → `Bad`
3. If no test is interpretable, the result is `Undefined`.

The resulting string (`Good`, `Uncertain`, `Bad`, `Severe`, `Undefined` or
`Error`) is what `quality.summary` — and hence the `TotalQ` column —
contains.

Note that `TotalQ` reflects the model as a whole. It can change when the
regression model changes even if the individual values of `Q` and `Q2` move
only slightly, because the classification of many tests contributes to the
average. Conversely, a single `Severe` test (for example a strong residual
trading day effect) is enough to make the overall summary `Severe`.

# Example

```{r example}
library(persephone3)

obj <- perX13(AirPassengers, "rsa3")
obj$run()

diagnosticsTable(obj)[, c("Q", "Q2", "TotalQ")]
```

With the default thresholds, `Q` and `Q2` values well below 1 (as is typical
for a clean multiplicative series like `AirPassengers`) are classified as
`Good` on their own, and if the other diagnostic groups are also unproblematic,
the overall summary `TotalQ` is `Good` as well.
